chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from a man who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Those who mixed a good deed and another evil one — so those are a people of faith who are innovating in their faith from the sins that the believers censure and dislike. So those are the ones upon whom Allah may turn (mercifully).'
ai.seo_question: Who are the Companions of the Heights (Ahl al-A'raf) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'Companions of the Heights' are true believers whose faith is not nullified by sins, but rather marred by them, which they themselves dislike and which the community censures. This interpretation aligns with the Shia view of intermediate spiritual states, distinguishing them from those who persist in sin without remorse. The hadith emphasizes the potential for divine mercy and repentance, offering hope for those who mix righteousness with minor transgressions.
